source_reports.citation: Sando, S.K., 1998, Techniques for estimating peak-flow magnitude and frequency relations for South Dakota streams: U.S. Geological Survey Water-Resources Investigations Report 98-4055, iv, 48 p.

notes: Sando, WRI 98-4055 (1998), the report NSS uses for South Dakota (citation 128), with data through water year 1994. NSS gives it another title, 'A Method for Estimating Magnitude and Frequency of Floods in South Dakota'; the citation here is the report's own. The PDF is born digital, not a scan: its table text was parsed and Table 4, Table 5 and samples of Tables 6 and 7 were read against page images. Neither the publication page nor the report lists a revision. Seven subregions at seven recurrence intervals, 2-500 years, stored as AEP = 1/T (0.5, 0.2, 0.1, 0.04, 0.02, 0.01, 0.002). Variables are CA = CONTDA (contributing drainage area), PII = PII_SD (the 2-year 24-hour precipitation intensity minus 1.5 in., to be read only from the report's figure 5, p. 19) and S = CSL10_85 (slope between 10 and 85 percent of length, Table 1). Constants are printed, so intercept = log10 of the constant. Ranges from Table 5, and all of Table 4's other columns: n_sites, SEP in percent, equivalent years. Subregion C uses 48 gages to 10 years and 46 from 25 years, since Table 6 has no such flows at 06399300 and 06400875. model_error_variance is Table 4's standard error of estimate, which the report defines as the model error (p. 14), converted from percent as ln(1 + (p/100)^2)/ln(10)^2. Covariance from Table 7, order Constant, CA, then PII or S, as printed; the report's GLS fit is in log10 of each. There is no site-specific worked example: the check on Table 7 is sqrt(mean(MEV + xUx)) over each subregion's Table 6 gages, which reproduces Table 4's average SEP in all 49 equations within the rounding of the printed percents. Every coefficient, constant, range and SEP equals NSS. Worked examples reproduce: Mosquito Creek (subregion B, 1,080 ft3/s), Willow Creek by procedure 2 (C 4,730, D 24,400, area-weighted 9,190) and 06477400's regression estimate (100). Table 6 prints no regression flows, only station and weighted flows; equation 4 with Table 4's average equivalent years reproduces all but the cells below of its 1,371 weighted flows, at 197 gages, within the rounding of what is printed. Table 6 prints 06478250's 25-year weighted flow as 55, where equation 4 gives 525 and the neighbouring flows are 237 and 867, so that is a misprint for a flow not stored here. 06453400's weighted flows imply 13 years of record where Table 6 prints 14. Six other cells, at 06446250 (two), 06355000, 06408500, 06354882 and 06334000, miss by about 1 percent or less. Table 6's largest subregion F slope is 460.1 where Table 5 prints 460. The report says to use extreme caution with subregion D above 15 mi2, because of unusually large estimates, though its range runs to 137 mi2; that limit is not enforced here, and C and D are interspersed, so a caller may need to choose with region=. It also warns about subregion G's large errors (7 gages) and about F and G sites just below limestone outcrops. Drainage-area transfers (equation 5) use mean exponents A 0.529, B 0.615, C 0.569, D 0.545, E 0.691, F 0.654, G 0.689, not used by the evaluator. A basin in more than one subregion is averaged in flow, not in log, by contributing area (procedure 2, p. 21), which weighting_space 'linear' makes the default here; Willow Creek's 9,190 would be about 6,860 in log. A caller's weighting_space overrides it.
